types.name: Fenrir::ChangeError
types.doc: What a script asked for that the change buffer refused at once: the result of every native that records a structural change. C# throws on anything but None, with a message that says which change was attempted, so one value serves a component and a resource alike. Described for the C# binding, so the values are the contract's.

values.name: None
values.doc: The change was recorded, to play back when the system returns.

values.name: EntityNotAlive
values.doc: The entity is not alive in the active scene.

values.name: Unknown
values.doc: No component, event or resource has the id.

values.name: ReadOnly
values.doc: Scripts may only read the component or resource, so they cannot add, remove, insert or remove it.

values.name: Required
values.doc: The engine needs every entity to have the component (Transform, Name, Relationship), so it cannot be removed.

values.name: NotActive
values.doc: Scripting is not running, so there is no scene to change.

types.name: Fenrir::EntityValue
types.doc: A C# Entity: an entity's 32-bit value alone. The wrapper a native takes or returns where C# passes an Entity, and the field a shared struct holds where C# holds one.

types.name: Fenrir::RegistryError
types.doc: Why a lookup of a component, event or resource by name gave no id. A lookup native returns the id when it found one, otherwise one of these; the binding's generated enum lets C# name the reason it throws for. Described for the C# binding (api/FenrirScripting.api.toml), so the values below are the contract's.

values.name: NotRegistered
values.doc: Nothing is registered under the name.

values.name: WrongType
values.doc: The name is registered for a different C# type than the one asking, so the layout check would be skipped.
